body:
I've successfully duplicated this issue on my machine. 

The trick here seems to be using the context menu to remove the scene in question instead of the Delete key. Using the delete key removes the referenced scene, but right clicking and choosing "Remove" does not, allowing for the scene to be renamed and thus crash OBS.

Thanks for the report!

This crash happens with any action taken on the now deleted scene. Moving, properties, filters, etc will all freeze and then crash. Below is a crash log from a successful repro - the steps are the same except for the final step where I simply dragged the scene item down, which somehow added it to a nonexistent group.

[Crash 2020-04-01 11-53-22.txt](https://github.com/obsproject/obs-studio/files/4414306/Crash.2020-04-01.11-53-22.txt)

labels.name: Confirmed

repository.name: obs-studio

issue.body:
<!-- READ THIS FIRST -->
<!-- The OBS Studio GitHub issue tracker is **ONLY** to be -->
<!-- used for reporting Bugs that have replication steps. -->

<!-- You can post Feature Requests here: https://ideas.obsproject.com/ -->
<!-- Get help for Support Issues here: https://obsproject.com/help -->

<!--- Provide a general summary of the issue in the Title above -->

## Platform
<!-- Please fill out the following information about your bug report. -->
<!-- If you are on Linux and installed using a package, please list the package type. -->
Operating system and version:  Windows 10 x64 (1909)
OBS Studio version:  25.0.4

## Expected Behavior
<!--- Tell us what should happen -->
When a scene is deleted in the scenes pane, Scene Source that refer to it in other scenes should either be changed to not refer to it and stay present, or they should be deleted from the sources list for any scenes they appear in.

## Current Behavior
<!--- Tell us what happens instead of the expected behavior. -->
When deleting a scene that is used elsewhere in a scene source, OBS sometimes still shows the scene source as being present and continues to refer to the scene that was deleted.

<!--- Please include a log file here if possible. -->
https://obsproject.com/logs/wwYQr1_Xulb08lMi

## Steps to Reproduce
<!--- Provide a link to a live example, or an unambiguous set of steps to -->
<!--- reproduce this bug. Include code to reproduce, if relevant. -->
<!--- Screenshots and video are encouraged if applicable. -->
1.  Create a new scene collection "Bug Test"
2.  Add a new scene named "Scene 2", and another named "Scene 3"
3.  Switch to the default "Scene", and add Scene Source "Scene 2", then another for "Scene 3"
4.  In the Scenes pane, select Scene 3, right click and Remove it.
5.  Now do the same and remove Scene 2 from the scenes pane.

OBS now shows the remaining original scene named "Scene" with one of the scenes that were previously deleted still showing up in the sources list.

## Additional information
<!--- Not obligatory, but provide any additional details or information -->
<!--- that you feel might be relevant to the issue -->
